n48d3f777a9a.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh recorded the highest level of urbanisation in Census 2011?
n48d3f777a9a.x: Visakhapatnam was the most urbanised district at 47.45%, followed by Krishna (40.81%); Srikakulam was the lowest at 16.16%.

n051bca83762.s: How many census towns did India have in Census 2011?
n051bca83762.x: Census towns rose from 1,362 (2001) to 3,894 (2011); the 7,935 towns of 2011 comprised 4,041 statutory and 3,894 census towns.

n9a155be730a.s: EAC-PM satellite data suggest India's urbanisation in 2015 could have been about:
n9a155be730a.x: EAC-PM satellite data put urbanisation at about 63% in 2015 against the Census figure of 31%; 55.3% is the World Bank 'urban-like' estimate and 41% the 16th Finance Commission's 2031 projection.

n5750c73de7c.s: Which of the following is one of the three processes of urbanisation identified by Rakesh Mohan?
n5750c73de7c.x: Rakesh Mohan identified metropolitanisation, commercialisation and rural or subsistence urbanisation.

nd1a656c15ea.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Negrito – Onge, Jarawa and Great Andamanese
Proto-Australoid – Nagas, Lepchas and Tibetans of Sikkim
Mongoloid – Shompen and Tibetans of Sikkim
Nordic – Punjab, Rajasthan and North-West Frontier
nd1a656c15ea.x: Nagas, Lepchas and Tibetans of Sikkim are Mongoloid; the Proto-Australoid group is represented by Santhal, Bhil, Chenchu, Munda and Ho.

n9f99ac65cde.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about scholars of racial classification in India?
o: S.S. Sarkar used the cephalic index
The nasal index was Risley's measure
Haddon classified populations mainly on the basis of the cephalic index
J.H. Hutton (Census Commissioner, 1931) held that India was peopled by successive waves of migration
n9f99ac65cde.x: Haddon classified populations by hair form (leiotrichi, cymotrichi, ulotrichi), not the cephalic index.

n42d2f308380.s:
Assertion (A): Risley's dictum stated that the social status of a caste varied inversely with its nasal index.
Reason (R): Risley treated a higher nasal index as indicating higher social status.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n42d2f308380.x: Risley's dictum stated an inverse relationship between caste status and nasal index; it did not treat a higher nasal index as indicating higher status. The dictum is now rejected as colonial race science.

n88c2f58d196.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
n88c2f58d196.s: In the 2009 genetic framework of Indian ancestry, 'ASI' stands for:
n88c2f58d196.x: Most Indians are described as a mixture of ANI (Ancestral North Indians) and ASI (Ancestral South Indians).

nea44ce3590f.s: The People of India project, launched in 1985, was led by:
nea44ce3590f.x: The People of India project was launched in 1985 under K.S. Singh and documented about 4,635 communities.

n95b7e5b52a6.s: B.S. Guha's racial classification of the Indian population was based on the data of which Census?
n95b7e5b52a6.x: Guha's classification, the most widely cited, was based on 1931 Census data and gave 6 main racial groups with 9 sub-types.

n13d59f6d4f4.s: In which year did India ratify the ICERD?
n13d59f6d4f4.x: India ratified ICERD in 1968; the UN CERD recently reviewed India for the first time since 2007.

n4ec32dde349.s: The tribal population of the Andaman Islands is associated with which racial stock?
n4ec32dde349.x: The Andaman tribes are Negrito, regarded as a sub-race of the Negroid group; the Shompen of Nicobar are Mongoloid.

ndb36de41112.s: The Anthropological Survey of India was founded in 1945 at:
ndb36de41112.x: AnSI was founded at Varanasi in 1945 and moved to Kolkata in 1948; B.S. Guha was its first Director.

n12cd6ee6401.s: How many racial types did Risley's classification of the Indian population have?
n12cd6ee6401.x: Risley gave seven types; Guha gave six main groups (with nine sub-types).

nworld-geography-27-5.s: Chinese, Japanese, Koreans, Mongols and American Indians are associated with which racial group?
nworld-geography-27-5.x: These peoples are associated with the Mongoloid group; Europeans, Arabs, Persians and many North Indians are Caucasoid.

nworld-geography-27-9.s: Aboriginal Australians and some Melanesians are associated with which racial group?
nworld-geography-27-9.x: The Australoid group includes Aboriginal Australians and some Melanesians.

nd1052f3baea.s: A high nasal bridge and a narrow nose are characteristic of which racial group?
nd1052f3baea.x: Caucasoids have a high bridge and narrow nose; Mongoloids a low-to-medium bridge; Negroids a low bridge and broad nose.

nda902a4e05a.s: Under Risley's classification, Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir were associated with which type?
nda902a4e05a.x: Risley linked Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir to the Indo-Aryan type; Scytho-Dravidian was linked to western India (Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Coorg).

n86fd5adcaef.s: Which of the following pairs (Andhra Pradesh body – 2024-25 fact) is NOT correctly matched?
o: AP State Haj Committee – 1,652 pilgrims approved for Haj 2025
AP State Minorities Finance Corporation – Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance
AP State Waqf Board – ₹10,000 per month to Imams and ₹5,000 to Mouzzans
AP State Christian Minorities Finance Corporation – ₹150.92 crore allocation
n86fd5adcaef.x: Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance belongs to the Christian Minorities Finance Corporation; the Minorities Finance Corporation handled post-matric RTF of ₹36.34 crore to 50,767 beneficiaries.

n47ee0e38f1b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the central minority scholarship schemes?
o: 50% of the scholarships are earmarked for girls
The Pre-matric Scholarship covers Classes IX and X
The Post-matric Scholarship has a parental income ceiling of Rs 2.5 lakh
The Merit-cum-Means Scholarship (2007) is for professional and technical UG-PG courses
n47ee0e38f1b.x: Payment is through NSP 2.0 and DBT, but 30% (not 50%) is earmarked for girls.

nc964d1b0081.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the classification of religions in Census 2011?
o: Six major religions were counted separately
Other Religions and Persuasions was recorded separately
A 'No Religion' option was already available in earlier Censuses
Religion Not Stated was recorded separately
nc964d1b0081.x: The 'No Religion' option was added for the first time in 2011, so it was not available earlier.

n08e6127c304.s:
Assertion (A): The Hindu share of India's population was below 80% in Census 2011.
Reason (R): The Hindu share fell from 80.5% in 2001 to 79.8% in 2011.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n08e6127c304.x: The Hindu share fell from 80.5% to 79.8% between 2001 and 2011, which is why it was below 80% in 2011.

n053aa119400.s: The Muslim share of India's population rose from about 10 per cent in 1951 to about ____ in 2011.
n053aa119400.x: The Muslim share rose from about 10% (1951) to about 14% (2011), attributed to poorer economic status and lower female education rather than religion.

nef0a35647bc.s: In which is the only State where Sikhs constitute a majority?
nef0a35647bc.x: Punjab is the only Sikh-majority State.

n2c54ab3708e.s: According to Census 2011, Christians formed what share of India's population?
n2c54ab3708e.x: Christians were 2.3%; Muslims 14.2%, Sikhs 1.7% and Jains 0.4%.

nb789ecf79a6.s: Which State has the largest number of Buddhists in India?
nb789ecf79a6.x: Maharashtra has the most Buddhists, following Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur in 1956.

n31b8d69066f.s: According to APSES 2024-25, which of the following describes the minority population of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Mostly urban, with a large BPL segment
Mostly rural, with a small BPL segment
Mostly urban, with a high share in economic support schemes
Mostly rural, with a high share in economic support schemes
n31b8d69066f.x: APSES 2024-25 describes AP's minority population as mostly urban, with a large BPL segment and a low share in economic support schemes.

nb05ea1075f3.s: According to Census 2011, India's literacy rate was:

nindian-geography-21-11.s: Scheduled Tribes formed what percentage of India's population in Census 2011?
nindian-geography-21-11.x: STs formed 8.6% and SCs 16.6% of the population in 2011; the child sex ratio (0-6) was 919.

nbac2aa30f96.s: According to Census 2011, which of the following religious communities had the smallest population?
nbac2aa30f96.x: In ascending order: Jain, Buddhist, Sikh, Christian, Muslim, Hindu.

n9baf4472c6f.s: In residual Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011), Muslims accounted for about what share of the population?
n9baf4472c6f.x: In residual AP, Hindus were about 90.9%, Muslims about 7.3% and Christians about 1.4%.

n486cc9330b0.s: Which religious community had the highest sex ratio in India in 2011?
n486cc9330b0.x: Christians had 1,023, followed by Buddhists (965), Jains (954), Muslims (951), Hindus (939) and Sikhs (903).

n7ebafd5ea8e.s: Which of the following is associated with the early arrival of Islam in India?
n7ebafd5ea8e.x: Islam arrived with Arab merchants and spread through the Turkish Sultanate, Mughals and Sufis; St Thomas, the Portuguese and Francis Xavier are linked to Christianity.

n25062a015d9.s: Over the long run, which religious community's share of India's population has steadily risen?
n25062a015d9.x: The Muslim share has steadily risen, the Hindu share has slowly declined, and Sikh and Buddhist shares have dipped.

nee025cfa0a0.s: What is the Christian population of Andhra Pradesh as officially stated?
nee025cfa0a0.x: AP's Christian population is 6.82 lakh; the State has a State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations, a Waqf Board, and Urdu as second official language.

n29836eaf13d.s: How much does Andhra Pradesh allocate annually for Imams and Mouzams?
n29836eaf13d.x: The annual allocation for Imams and Mouzams is ₹180 crore; Urdu was declared the second official language of AP.

n57a417e58bc.s: In the first detailed census of 1881, religions of Indian origin formed about what share of the population?
n57a417e58bc.x: Religions of Indian origin were about 79% of the population in 1881, and about 95% of them were Hindus; Christians were about 0.7%.

n6274fe13b99.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revised (2024) criteria for classical languages?
o: Knowledge texts were added to the scope of eligible literature
The requirement that the tradition be 'original, not borrowed' was retained
Both prose and poetry were recognised
Epigraphic evidence was added as a consideration
n6274fe13b99.x: The 2024 revision dropped the 'original, not borrowed' requirement.

n767482db0bf.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 344 – Union's duty to develop Hindi
Article 343 – Hindi in Devanagari as official language of the Union
Article 345 – State Legislature adopts the official language(s) of the State
Article 351 – Union's duty to develop Hindi
n767482db0bf.x: Article 344 provides for the President's Official Language Commission and Parliamentary Committee; the duty to develop Hindi is Article 351.

nf1ceaa6e801.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's language-family shares?
o: The older estimate for Indo-Aryan was about 73 per cent
The 2011 estimate for Dravidian was about 19.64 per cent
The older estimate for Tibeto-Burman was about 20 per cent
The 2011 estimate for Indo-Aryan was about 78.05 per cent
nf1ceaa6e801.x: The older Tibeto-Burman estimate was about 0.85 per cent, not 20 per cent (20 per cent was the older Dravidian figure).

ne41f19719c4.s: Which of the following pairs (Eighth Schedule) is NOT correctly matched?
ne41f19719c4.x: The 71st Amendment (1992) added three languages: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; the 92nd added four.

nec418b9c373.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage?
nec418b9c373.x: Article 350A deals with mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage; Article 350 covers representations for redress in any language.

nef323f1d124.s: Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks the birth anniversary of:
nef323f1d124.x: 29 August is Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy's birth anniversary; he led the Vyavaharika (colloquial) Telugu movement and designed a script for Savara.

n6340280e493.s: The Kalamalla inscription (575 CE), regarded as the first fully Telugu inscription, was issued by the:
n6340280e493.x: The Kalamalla inscription of 575 CE, in Kadapa, was issued by the Renati Cholas; the earliest Telugu word 'Nagabu' is in the Amaravati inscription.

n5a272683b46.s: Under the Munshi-Ayyangar formula (adopted 14 September 1949), Hindi in Devanagari was to become the Union's official language after a transition of:
n5a272683b46.x: The formula provided a 15-year transition; its adoption date, 14 September, is observed as Hindi Diwas.

nb52e46055ce.s: The Koya tribal language of Andhra Pradesh is mainly spoken in the:
nb52e46055ce.x: Koya is spoken in the Godavari agency; Savara in the Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills, Kui/Kuvi on the AP-Odisha border hills and Gadaba in the Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency.

nc6247b1883a.s: The Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages (SPPEL) is run by:
o: Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysuru
nc6247b1883a.x: SPPEL, a Union Education Ministry scheme of 2013, is run by CIIL, Mysuru and covers languages with fewer than 10,000 speakers.

nae653808663.s: Telugu is classified under which branch of the Dravidian language family?
nae653808663.x: Telugu is South-Central Dravidian; Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam are southern, while Kui, Gondi and Kurukh are Central or North Dravidian.

nworld-geography-29-5.s: In India, Austro-Asiatic (Austric) languages are mainly spoken in:
o: Central and East India and Meghalaya
nworld-geography-29-5.x: Austro-Asiatic is spoken in central-east India and Meghalaya; Dravidian in the south, Indo-European in the north, west and east, and Sino-Tibetan in the north-east and Himalayas.

nd4880f796af.s: In Census 2011, the 1,369 rationalised mother tongues were grouped into how many languages?
nd4880f796af.x: The 1,369 mother tongues were grouped into 121 languages: 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled.

n4f927cf57d5.s: According to Census 2011, about what percentage of Indians were bilingual?
n4f927cf57d5.x: About 26% were bilingual and only about 7% trilingual in Census 2011.

n24d024e8e2b.s: Under the Constitution, the official language(s) of a State are adopted by the:
n24d024e8e2b.x: Each State may choose its own official language(s) through its Legislature; a State is not required to adopt Hindi as its only official language.

n219088ab2c8.s: The Sitakant Mohapatra Committee on inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule was constituted in:
n219088ab2c8.x: The Sitakant Mohapatra Committee was constituted in 2003 and the Ashok Pahwa Committee in 1996; there are no fixed criteria for inclusion.

n6c5a1cfea17.s: How many classical languages does India have?
n6c5a1cfea17.x: India has 11 classical languages; Pali and Prakrit are the only ones outside the Eighth Schedule.

ne03883fab21.s: Telugu was recognised as a classical language in:
ne03883fab21.x: Telugu, a Dravidian language and one of the 22 scheduled languages, became a classical language in 2008.

n05aacf07049.s: In which year was Sindhi added to the Eighth Schedule?
n05aacf07049.x: Sindhi was added in 1967 (21st Amendment); the Telugu Language Act was 1966, Tamil became the first classical language in 2004 and Telugu in 2008.

nworld-geography-29-4.s: Romani, the language originally spoken by the Gypsies (Roma), is related to which languages?
nworld-geography-29-4.x: Romani is related to the Indo-Aryan languages of India.

nworld-geography-28-9.s: The Bantu languages belong to which language family?
nworld-geography-28-9.x: The Niger-Congo family, spread across Sub-Saharan Africa, includes the Bantu languages.

nworld-geography-28-8.s: Which language family is the second largest by number of speakers?
nworld-geography-28-8.x: Sino-Tibetan is the second largest family by speakers; Cantonese, Tibetan and Burmese are among its major languages.

na5d346d0543.s: According to Census 2011, which language had the second largest share of speakers in India after Hindi?
na5d346d0543.x: Hindi (43.6%) was followed by Bengali (8.0%); Telugu had 6.7% and Tamil 5.7%.

n16fde836ea7.s: Which language was the first to be recognised as a classical language of India?
n16fde836ea7.x: Tamil was recognised in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Kannada in 2008 and Odia in 2014.

ndd6b3060340.s: Which script is the Centre encouraging for North-Eastern tribal languages that have no script of their own?
ndd6b3060340.x: The Centre has been pushing Devanagari for script-less North-Eastern tribal languages; Tripura's CPI(M) opposed the move.

nfedfb7d71da.s: Which of the following languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule?
nfedfb7d71da.x: Bhojpuri, like Kokborok and Gor Boli (Lambadi), is not in the Eighth Schedule; Konkani and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment.

n54f2c5d9cff.s: For Census language classification, a language generally needs at least how many speakers?
n54f2c5d9cff.x: The Census counts a language when it has 10,000 or more speakers.

nde3efc8e81d.s: About how many Indian languages are listed in UNESCO's Atlas of Endangered Languages?
nde3efc8e81d.x: India has about 197 languages in UNESCO's Atlas, the highest for any country.

n5c595f3fd96.s: With regard to the Eighth Schedule, English has:
n5c595f3fd96.x: English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.

ne7e8683f145.s:
Assertion (A): The World Migration Report is published by the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
Reason (R): The World Migration Report has been brought out every year since 2000.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne7e8683f145.x: IOM publishes the report (2026 is the 13th edition), but it is biennial since 2000, not annual.

nb7414acd692.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
nb7414acd692.s: Under the Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979, an establishment had to register if it employed ____ or more inter-State migrant workers.
nb7414acd692.x: Registration was required for establishments with 5 or more inter-State migrant workers; workers got a displacement allowance of 50% of monthly wages plus a journey allowance.

n8aeb4293f38.s: As a demographic consequence of out-migration, the source area is often left with:
o: a younger population and more men
an ageing population and more men
a younger population and more women
an ageing population and more women
n8aeb4293f38.x: Population falls at the source, which is left with ageing people and a higher share of women.

n538e991ef7d.s: One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) is operational in how many States/UTs?
n538e991ef7d.x: ONORC, giving NFSA ration portability, works in all 36 States/UTs.

n456c2f9a8e1.s: PLFS/NSO treat a place as the Usual Place of Residence if a person has lived there for at least:
n456c2f9a8e1.x: The PLFS/NSO rule is at least 6 months; the Census uses both place of birth (lifetime migrants) and place of last residence.

n668a63d17a4.s: According to PLFS 2020-21, India's overall migration rate was:
n668a63d17a4.x: The overall rate was 28.9%; the female rate was 47.9% and the male rate 10.7%.

n604d1b0256d.s: By place of last residence, about what share of India's population were migrants in Census 2011?
n604d1b0256d.x: 455.8 million people, about 37.6% of the population, were migrants by place of last residence; 141.2 million had moved during 2001-11.

n4f7639af1eb.s: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was endorsed by the:
n4f7639af1eb.x: The UN General Assembly endorsed the Compact; it is non-binding and covers international migration, not internal displacement.

nf1f7135b72b.s: The e-Shram portal is available in 22 languages through:
nf1f7135b72b.x: e-Shram's 22-language support comes through BHASHINI; it is a One-Stop-Solution linked to 15 central schemes.

n6d7f2d95b97.s: About how many jobs were lost in India during the COVID-19 lockdown?
n6d7f2d95b97.x: About 122 million jobs were lost; the lockdown exposed job insecurity, wage exploitation and the absence of social security for migrants.

nf8d36eaf90d.s: The migrants from Konaseema to the GCC countries (about 15,000 by December 2025) were mostly:
nf8d36eaf90d.x: Over 70 per cent of the Konaseema migrants were women, mostly working as housemaids, and cases of exploitation were reported.

n70abb091c5d.s: About how many Indians live in the United Arab Emirates?
n70abb091c5d.x: About 3.5 million Indians are in the UAE; India has the world's largest diaspora, over 35 million.

n0078eec6905.s: Which of the following can encourage rural-to-urban migration?
n0078eec6905.x: Rural-urban migration is encouraged by high urban labour demand, unbalanced rural-urban development and lack of rural employment.

nb178798559e.s: The four Labour Codes, including the OSH Code, consolidated how many laws?
nb178798559e.x: The four Labour Codes consolidated 29 laws and came into force in November 2025.

n678d116b5b1.s: The mobility transition model of migration is associated with:
n678d116b5b1.x: Zelinsky gave the mobility transition model; Ravenstein the laws of migration and Griffith Taylor the migration zone theory.

n42238513931.s: Under the revised MoSPI definition, short-term migration covers a stay away of:
n42238513931.x: The revised definition covers 15 days–6 months; the earlier one covered 1–6 months.

ndd2191a175f.s: Intra-state rural-to-rural migration in India is dominated by:
ndd2191a175f.x: Women dominate intra-state rural-to-rural movements linked to marriage, while men dominate inter-state rural-to-urban movements for work.

n83232b44a8d.s: Which country has the highest share of international migrants in its population?
n83232b44a8d.x: The UAE has the highest migrant share; Europe has the largest number of migrants and Oceania the highest percentage.

n033da2c93de.s:
Assertion (A): During 2001-11, for the first time since Independence, the absolute increase in urban population exceeded the rural increase.
Reason (R): India's urban population grew by about 41.8% during 2001-11.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n033da2c93de.x: Urban areas added about 91 million, more than rural areas, a first since Independence; but urban population rose from 286 to 377.1 million, about 31.8%, not 41.8%.

n67dd396ef06.s: The EAC-PM estimate of about 63% urbanisation in India in 2015 was based on:
n67dd396ef06.x: The EAC-PM's 63% figure came from satellite data; the World Bank (2010) put 55.3% in urban-like areas.

n46c89a6cb8e.s: UN-Habitat's World Cities Report 2026 was released at the World Urban Forum in:
n46c89a6cb8e.x: It was released at the World Urban Forum, Baku; it says about 40% (about 3.4 billion) face housing shortages and about 1.1 billion live in slums.

n82827c4632e.s: Which was the most urbanised State in India in Census 2011?
n82827c4632e.x: Goa (62.17%) was the most urbanised State and Himachal Pradesh (10.04%) the least; NCT of Delhi (97.50%) was highest overall.

n45de41b9222.s: The rapid phase of urban growth in India began in:
n45de41b9222.x: 1901-31 was the slow phase and 1931-61 the medium phase; the rapid phase began in 1961, with urban population rising from 78.94 to 377.11 million.

nbe3f9c29a98.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added which Schedule to the Constitution?
nbe3f9c29a98.x: It inserted Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 functions for urban local bodies) and came into force on 1 June 1993.

n6bd937e81be.s: The criticism that Indian cities are 'administered, not governed' points to:
o: too many agencies and low own-source revenue of ULBs
too few agencies and high own-source revenue of ULBs
a single agency controlling all urban services
n6bd937e81be.x: The criticism points to a proliferation of agencies (ULBs and parastatals) and low own-source revenue, not an absence of municipal institutions.

n02a77ed4925.s: Among the 2011 urban agglomerations, which of the following was NOT a mega city?
n02a77ed4925.x: Only Greater Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata had 10 million or more; Chennai had about 8.7 million.

n2b60704d767.s: Which city of Andhra Pradesh was among the 12 HRIDAY cities?
n2b60704d767.x: Amaravati was one of the 12 cities of HRIDAY (2015), the heritage city development scheme; HRIDAY cities are covered under AMRUT.

n1258e0e1110.s: The 100 cities of the Smart Cities Mission were selected in how many rounds?
n1258e0e1110.x: The 100 cities were chosen in four rounds (Jan 2016-Jun 2018); the Mission was launched in 2015 as a CSS, and Visakhapatnam is one of them.

na804d48cd7e.s: Natural increase, net rural-urban migration and ____ are the three components of urban growth.
o: reclassification of rural areas as urban
na804d48cd7e.x: The three components are natural increase, rural-urban migration and reclassification of rural areas as urban (creation of new towns).

n50190d8195a.x: AMRUT was launched on 25 June 2015, covering 500 cities (485 after mergers), with an outlay of ₹1 lakh crore.

n2a02f95988c.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 describes Indian cities as:
n2a02f95988c.x: The Survey (Ch. 15) calls cities 'critical economic infrastructure'; it says they have population scale but lack liveability.

n371d308eee4.s: UN-Habitat, set up in 1978, is headquartered at:
n371d308eee4.x: UN-Habitat is headquartered in Nairobi; the related AP initiative is a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at Amaravati.

n1dd4e9e5509.s: Which cities were listed in the Super Swachh League (10 lakh+ population) of Swachh Survekshan?
n1dd4e9e5509.x: Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai were in the 10 lakh+ Super Swachh League; Noida, Chandigarh and Mysuru in its 3-10 lakh category.

na69987dedab.s: A chain of merged metropolitan areas is known as a:
na69987dedab.x: A megalopolis is a chain of merged metropolitan areas; a conurbation is a continuous urban area formed by merging towns.

n9ef28cf91b4.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the growth of 16 major Indian cities during 2000-2020 has been:
o: horizontal, with the periphery growing faster than the core
vertical, with the core growing faster than the periphery
horizontal, with the core growing faster than the periphery
vertical, with the periphery growing faster than the core
n9ef28cf91b4.x: The periphery grew faster than the core and expansion was predominantly horizontal; the administrative city no longer matches the economic metropolitan region.

n92f79c78b25.s: Among million-plus cities in Census 2011, the highest share of slum households was in:
n92f79c78b25.x: Greater Visakhapatnam (about 44%) was ahead of Mumbai (about 41%), though Greater Mumbai had the largest slum population.

n25414015af5.s: Swachh Survekshan began in 2016 with how many cities?
n25414015af5.x: It began in 2016 with 73 cities; run by MoHUA and conducted by QCI, the 2024-25 survey covered 4,589 cities.

n5fc068d5253.s: India generates about how much municipal solid waste a year?
n5fc068d5253.x: India generates about 62 million tonnes of MSW a year; about 70% is collected but only 30% processed.

ndd38413fa40.s: The Chennai Metropolitan Area is planned by:
ndd38413fa40.x: Chennai is planned by CMDA (1974); KMDA (1970) is Kolkata's, VMRDA plans Visakhapatnam and APCRDA plans Amaravati.

n2b83abc597b.s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, which is the world's most populous city?
n2b83abc597b.x: The order is Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi.

nb981f8cd996.s: Which of the following is a major cause of urban flooding in expanding cities?
o: Construction over lakes, wetlands and floodplains
nb981f8cd996.x: Urban flooding is caused by construction over water bodies and floodplains, concretisation of permeable soil and blocked drains.

n483d578e8ed.s: Which of the following States is NOT a participating unit of the National Capital Region?
n483d578e8ed.x: The NCR comprises NCT of Delhi and parts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan; Punjab is not part of it.

nf79a7d3eb34.s: In Census 2011, which State had the highest share of its urban population living in slums?
nf79a7d3eb34.x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh had the highest share, at about 36%.

n47df971de92.s: Which index is the ratio of female to male HDI?
n47df971de92.x: GDI is the female-to-male HDI ratio; GII covers reproductive health, empowerment and labour market; PQLI uses literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy.

n37e67c7f18d.s: Amartya Sen's book 'Development as Freedom' was published in:
n37e67c7f18d.x: 'Development as Freedom' came out in 1999; 1990 is the year of the first HDR, conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with Sen.

n6a597ba0886.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the lowest multidimensional poverty headcount ratio (2.42 per cent)?
n6a597ba0886.x: West Godavari had the lowest ratio at 2.42 per cent; AP's MPI halved from 0.053 to 0.025.

n083d30ed9e8.s: In the Gender Inequality Index (GII), a value of 0 denotes:
o: maximum inequality between women and men
female HDI higher than male HDI
male HDI higher than female HDI
n083d30ed9e8.x: On the GII scale, 0 = equality and 1 = worst outcome; the GDI (female-to-male HDI ratio) near 1 means parity.

nc38354a94f6.s: Since 2010, the three dimension indices of the HDI are combined using the:
nc38354a94f6.x: The HDI is the geometric mean of the three indices, which replaced the arithmetic mean in 2010.

n4341075e041.s: Unlike human development, which has both quantitative and qualitative dimensions, economic growth is primarily:
n4341075e041.x: Economic growth is primarily quantitative and associated with income.

n03a490406d9.s: Where inequality exists in a country, its Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI) is:
n03a490406d9.x: The IHDI discounts the HDI for inequality in each dimension, so it is lower when inequality exists and equals the HDI only when there is none.

nd24e3ce1951.s: Amartya Sen received the Nobel Prize in Economics in:
nd24e3ce1951.x: Sen received the Nobel in 1998; the human development approach views development as the enlargement of human choices.

nf585ebe5524.s: Which State has the lowest state HDI (0.650), against India's 0.685?
nf585ebe5524.x: Bihar records the lowest state HDI at 0.650; Kerala and Goa are above 0.86.

n418d181d2d2.s: The income dimension of the HDI is measured by:
n418d181d2d2.x: HDI uses GNI per capita; education uses mean years of schooling (25+) and expected years of schooling.

nb1c0a5841e3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about population growth in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Decadal growth in 1991–2001 was 12.32 per cent
Decadal growth in 2001–2011 was 9.21 per cent
In 2001–2011, AP grew at about half the national rate
AP's 1991–2001 growth was higher than India's 21.5 per cent
nb1c0a5841e3.x: AP's 12.32 per cent growth in 1991–2001 was below India's 21.5 per cent.

n86a245dcd3a.s: Which of the following pairs about Andhra Pradesh's population policy is correctly matched?
o: Target TFR of the draft policy – 1.5
n86a245dcd3a.x: The CM announced Rs 30,000 for the third child and Rs 40,000 for the fourth; the draft policy aims to raise TFR from 1.5 to 2.1, and 'Pillale Sampada' marks a shift to population promotion.

nd8190a8b920.s: In 2011, the 0–6 age-group population formed about what share of Andhra Pradesh's population?
nd8190a8b920.x: The 0–6 population was 52.44 lakh, about 10.6 per cent (India 13.1 per cent), down from 58.23 lakh in 2001.

ne843eae7304.s: Which was the most populous of Andhra Pradesh's 13 districts in Census 2011?
ne843eae7304.x: East Godavari was the most populous (about 51.5 lakh); Vizianagaram was the least populous (about 23.4 lakh).

nf8e902a624d.s: The number of households in Andhra Pradesh rose from 57.52 lakh in 1971 to ____ in 2011.
nf8e902a624d.x: Households rose to 127.19 lakh while average size fell from about 5 to about 3.9, consistent with nuclear families.

n65c1ca54e8f.s: What is India's total fertility rate (TFR), against Andhra Pradesh's 1.5?
n65c1ca54e8f.x: India's TFR is 1.9 and AP's 1.5, both below the replacement level of 2.1.

n34ff98f5ce3.s: According to NFHS-5, the total fertility rate of Andhra Pradesh was about:
n34ff98f5ce3.x: NFHS-5 gave AP a TFR of about 1.7; the figure of 1.5 is the SRS estimate.

n8b1f2eb6a5f.s: The coastline of Andhra Pradesh is about how long?
n8b1f2eb6a5f.x: AP's coastline is about 974 km, the third longest among States; its area is about 1,62,970 sq km.

n3f4cce50047.s: After the 2025 reorganisation into 28 districts, which district of Andhra Pradesh has the highest population density?
n3f4cce50047.x: Visakhapatnam has the highest density, about 1,870 per sq km; Polavaram has the lowest (54).

nc9a0e377ec1.s: What is the crude birth rate of Andhra Pradesh?
nc9a0e377ec1.x: AP's CBR is 15.0 against India's 18.4, while its CDR (6.9) is higher than India's (6.4).

n73930dd1776.s: The sex ratio of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011 was:
n73930dd1776.x: AP's sex ratio was 997, 54 points above India's 943.

n2d966580700.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the share of workers in agriculture?
o: India's latest figure is about 46.1 per cent
As per the Census, India's share rose from 54.6 per cent in 2001 to 58.2 per cent in 2011
As per PLFS 2023-24, about 45.6 per cent of AP's workers were in agriculture
AP's share is slightly below the latest national figure
n2d966580700.x: The Census share fell, from 58.2 per cent in 2001 to 54.6 per cent in 2011.

n4f60605574a.s: Which was the first State to be declared fully literate under ULLAS (New India Literacy Programme)?
n4f60605574a.x: Mizoram (2025) was the first State and Ladakh (2024) the first UT; the benchmark is 95%+ literacy among those aged 15+.

n8805ffd64b8.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh recorded the lowest literacy rate (44.67%)?
n8805ffd64b8.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju recorded 44.67%; AP's ST literacy was 48.8% against 67.35% overall.

n60c3176ba25.s: The Akshara Andhra literacy drive, linked to ULLAS, is meant for people aged:
n60c3176ba25.x: Akshara Andhra targets below-average districts and dovetails with ULLAS for people aged 15 and above.

na01f99e8b2f.s: According to the Civil Registration System (CRS) 2024, India's sex ratio at birth was:
na01f99e8b2f.x: CRS 2024 recorded a sex ratio at birth of 917; son preference is addressed by the PCPNDT Act, 1994.

n29099e9c80f.s: Which State recorded the lowest literacy rate in Census 2011?
n29099e9c80f.x: Bihar had the lowest literacy rate and Kerala the highest in Census 2011.

n3e6d4a328df.s: The gender literacy gap in Rajasthan, the widest compared with Andhra Pradesh (about 15) and India (16), was about:
n3e6d4a328df.x: The gap was about 15 points in AP, 16 nationally and 28 in Rajasthan.

ne31e0883f66.s:
Assertion (A): Podu cultivation in Andhra Pradesh causes soil erosion and forest fires.
Reason (R): Podu is practised mainly in the Nallamala hills of the Rayalaseema region.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne31e0883f66.x: Podu, a slash-and-burn shifting cultivation, causes soil erosion and forest fires; but it is practised in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam, not the Nallamala hills, where the Chenchus are hunter-gatherers.

ndb374b2c217.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
ndb374b2c217.s: Which State has the largest number of notified Scheduled Tribes (62)?
ndb374b2c217.x: Odisha has 62 notified tribes; under Article 342 the President notifies STs after consulting the Governor, and only Parliament can amend the list by law.

n51a526bda8c.s: About how many villages, mostly tribal, are expected to be submerged by the Polavaram project?
n51a526bda8c.x: About 276 villages, mostly tribal, in ASR and Eluru are to be submerged; Koya and Kondh groups oppose the displacement.

n45be1468ba0.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC) of Andhra Pradesh was set up in:
n45be1468ba0.x: The GCC was set up in 1956; 1973 is when the Dhebar Commission created the PTG category. The GCC procures MFP, runs interior PDS depots and owns the 'GCC Araku Valley Coffee' trademark.

n52a3c4eddb5.s: The '1/70 Regulation' of Andhra Pradesh bars transfer of land in Scheduled Areas:
o: from tribals to non-tribals and also between non-tribals
only from tribals to the government
n52a3c4eddb5.x: The AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1959, amended by Regulation 1 of 1970, bars transfers from tribals to non-tribals and also between non-tribals.

n3944ca786b5.s: The SC and ST Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976 notified how many Scheduled Tribes in undivided Andhra Pradesh?
n3944ca786b5.x: The 1976 Act notified 33 STs, five with area restrictions (Gowdu, Mali, Nayak, Thoti, Valmiki); APSES 2024-25 counts 34 ST communities in present AP.

nc26e0e33a2a.s: According to Census 2011, Scheduled Tribes formed what percentage of Andhra Pradesh's population?
nc26e0e33a2a.x: AP has 27.39 lakh STs, 5.53 per cent of its population; about 12.9 lakh tribals live in Scheduled Areas.

nd80fd7e3e9e.s: Which of the following is a plains tribe found in almost all plain districts of Andhra Pradesh?
nd80fd7e3e9e.x: The Yerukula are a plains tribe; Konda Kapu and Manna Dhora live in the northern hill and frontier areas, and Kulia and Rona in the northern agency tracts.

n2db55c56c30.s: Which tribe's name is traditionally taken to mean 'those who live under trees'?
n2db55c56c30.x: Chenchu means 'those who live under trees'; their origin myth is the marriage of Ahobilam Narasimha with Chenchita.

n71a57b47b15.s: The Yanadis of Andhra Pradesh live mainly in the:
o: southern coastal plains around Pulicat Lake
n71a57b47b15.x: Yanadis live on the southern coastal plains around Pulicat Lake; Nallamala is the Chenchu habitat, Konda Reddis live in the Godavari hill tracts and Konda Doras in the Visakhapatnam agency.

n210729bdffc.s: The traditional settlements of the Lambada (Sugali) community are called:
n210729bdffc.x: Lambadas live in thandas; once traders and transporters, they now practise agriculture and animal husbandry.

n5a9e957849f.s: The Primitive Tribal Group (PTG) category was renamed Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) in:
n5a9e957849f.x: PTGs became PVTGs in 2006; the Dhebar Commission created the PTG category in 1973.

nap-geography-5-5.s: Which tribe of Andhra Pradesh is associated with the Nallamala forests?
nap-geography-5-5.x: The Chenchu are the Nallamala tribe; Konda Dhora live in the northern Eastern Ghats, Kondh on the Odisha border, and Nakkala in plains and commercial areas.

nap-geography-5-11.s: The Yerukula tribe is traditionally associated with:
nap-geography-5-11.x: Yerukulas, found in almost every plains district of AP, traditionally made baskets and told fortunes.

nap-geography-5-4.s: The Yanadi tribe is associated with which area of Andhra Pradesh?
nap-geography-5-4.x: Yanadi live in the Nellore plains; Sugali (Lambadi, Banjara) are associated with Rayalaseema and central Andhra.

n966527ecfa1.s: How many PVTGs are listed for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana together?
n966527ecfa1.x: The Ministry's list has 12 PVTGs for AP and Telangana together; Odisha has 13 and India 75.

n600356d7297.s: Which of the following is a PVTG listed for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
n600356d7297.x: Konda Reddi, Thoti and Bodo Gadaba are in the 12-member PVTG list; Yerukula is a major tribe but not a PVTG.

n7418e28e4db.s: How many Scheduled Tribes were counted in Census 2011?
n7418e28e4db.x: Census 2011 counted 698, while more than 700 tribes are notified under Article 342, some overlapping more than one State.

nfbc1a6f9064.s: In Census 2011, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the largest Scheduled Tribe population?
nfbc1a6f9064.x: Visakhapatnam had the most STs in 2011; the relevant area is now the ASR district.

nccff360ba9d.s: Polavaram district, carved out of Alluri Sitharama Raju district on 31 December 2025, has its headquarters at:
nccff360ba9d.x: Its headquarters is Rampachodavaram; it holds the Rampachodavaram and Chintoor ITDAs.

nc591f1d31ca.s: Which is the most widely spoken Dravidian language?
nc591f1d31ca.x: Telugu is the most widely spoken Dravidian language; in 2011 it ranked 4th in India after Hindi, Bengali and Marathi.

ne25ce991e40.s: Classical Language status in India is granted by the:
ne25ce991e40.x: The Union Government grants the status; Tamil was first (2004), and Telugu and Kannada followed in 2008.

ne9798422afe.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about urban schemes?
o: The Smart Cities Mission was launched in June 2015 for 100 cities
The central share under the Smart Cities Mission was ₹1 lakh crore
AMRUT was extended up to September 2025
ne9798422afe.x: The Smart Cities central share was ₹48,000 crore; ₹1 lakh crore is the AMRUT outlay.

nf0f163048ff.s: In Census 2011, about what percentage of Andhra Pradesh's population was urban?
nf0f163048ff.x: AP was 29.47 per cent urban against India's 31.16 per cent, making it the least urbanised southern State.

n62b2ee52884.s: Which of the following is a million-plus urban agglomeration of Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011)?
n62b2ee52884.x: Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada are AP's million-plus agglomerations; Tirupati is a major centre but not million-plus.

nf4c2e93f5e0.s: VMRDA, which plans the Visakhapatnam metropolitan region, was formed in 2018 from:
nf4c2e93f5e0.x: VMRDA was formed from VUDA in 2018; APCRDA plans the Amaravati capital region.

n0b39c1de090.s: In Census 2011, undivided Andhra Pradesh had about how many slum dwellers?
n0b39c1de090.x: Undivided AP had about 1.02 crore slum dwellers, second after Maharashtra.

ne9d28112a49.s: Flash floods in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada are linked mainly to:
o: loss of wetlands and blocked drains
ne9d28112a49.x: Loss of wetlands and blocked drains reduce the capacity of these cities to absorb and convey excess water.

o: merging peri-urban villages into Urban Local Bodies
n26e46cfef1b.x: The Urbanisation Premium rewards the merger of peri-urban villages into Urban Local Bodies.

na98d9c005eb.s: Between 2001 and 2011, the urban population of Andhra Pradesh grew by about:
na98d9c005eb.x: Urban population rose from 109.56 lakh to 146.10 lakh (about 33%), while rural population grew only about 1.5%.

n2d65e6e0c8d.s: A census town needs a population of 5,000+, a density of 400+ per sq km, and at least ____ of male workers outside agriculture.
n2d65e6e0c8d.x: The Census criteria are at least 5,000 people, at least 75% of male workers outside agriculture and at least 400 persons per sq km.

ncee262f33b3.s: As per Census 2011, how many cities of Andhra Pradesh had a population of more than one lakh?
ncee262f33b3.x: The APPSC-GS 2019 key gives 32 cities with more than one lakh population in 2011.

n3f4dfa8726f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index?
o: It is prepared by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI
Headcount fell from 29.17 per cent (2013-14) to 11.28 per cent (2022-23)
It uses four dimensions and sixteen indicators
About 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty (NITI, January 2024)
n3f4dfa8726f.x: The National MPI uses three dimensions and twelve indicators.

ndbf39d0c57d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Talliki Vandanam?
o: It is the successor to Amma Vodi
It gives Rs 15,000 per child per year to the mother
It is calculated per child, not per mother
ndbf39d0c57d.x: Talliki Vandanam covers both government and private schools.

n93a3090a4a3.s: Which of the following pairs about the present HDI method is correctly matched?
o: Education – adult literacy rate and gross enrolment
Income – GNI per capita (PPP), entered as a logarithm
Combining the three indices – arithmetic mean
n93a3090a4a3.x: Income is GNI per capita (PPP) in log form; since 2010 education uses mean and expected years of schooling and the indices are combined by a geometric mean.

n705e34d8c20.s: Mission Antyodaya, which ranks gram panchayats through an annual survey, is a convergence framework of which Ministry?
n705e34d8c20.x: It is the Ministry of Rural Development's framework, not a healthcare mission; AP's state average score was 61.

n9ff56bcccb8.s: Among Andhra Pradesh's 28 districts (Census 2011 recast), which has the highest urbanisation?
n9ff56bcccb8.x: Visakhapatnam is most urbanised (89.69 per cent) and Polavaram least (2.84 per cent); SPSR Nellore is most populous.

ncfdd89ba439.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh ranked first on which goal?
ncfdd89ba439.x: AP was 1st on SDG 7, 2nd on SDG 14 and 3rd on SDG 1; Kerala and Uttarakhand topped the index at 79.

n5dc65c3def7.s: In the latest sub-national HDI comparison, Kerala (HDI above 0.86) ranks:
n5dc65c3def7.x: Kerala and Goa both have HDI values above 0.86, and Kerala ranks second.

n9d878638826.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about global sectoral patterns?
o: Services form about 70-80 per cent of GDP in developed countries
In developing countries the primary sector is still large in employment
In developing countries services grow faster than industry
In developed countries the quaternary and quinary sectors are shrinking
n9d878638826.x: The quaternary and quinary sectors are growing, not shrinking, in developed countries.

nca5d14138e1.s: Which of the following pairs about Andhra Pradesh's economy is correctly matched?
o: Manufacturing share of GSDP – about 33 per cent
nca5d14138e1.x: AP is services-led with manufacturing at about 11 per cent of GSDP; Industrial Policy 4.0 for 2024-29 seeks to fill this manufacturing 'missing middle'.

n420d6cc2bb1.s: The unorganised sector is characterised by:
n420d6cc2bb1.x: Small scattered units, irregular pay and lack of social security mark the unorganised sector; public/private is a separate classification by ownership.

nacd45f4a334.x: Pink collar means service jobs long held mostly by women; red collar is primary-sector outdoor work, blue collar manual work and white collar office work.

nf2bb3d0bde1.s: By the nature of the activity, mining is a ____ activity, though GVA reporting places it in the Industry sector.
nf2bb3d0bde1.x: Mining is primary because it extracts resources from nature; in GVA reporting it is grouped under Industry.

na7aa7f247e9.s: In both India and Andhra Pradesh, which sector accounts for the largest share of employment?
na7aa7f247e9.x: Agriculture leads in employment, while services have the largest GVA share.

n1b1c37c5922.s: Agriculture and allied activities contribute about what share of Andhra Pradesh's GVA?
n1b1c37c5922.x: Agriculture is about 33% of AP GVA against about 21% nationally, led by livestock and fisheries.

nbe7e0dac253.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about shifting cultivation?
o: It is found in high-rainfall forests of the Amazon, Tropical Africa, South-East Asia and North-East India
It is primitive subsistence, slash-and-burn agriculture
It is a capital-intensive, export-oriented commercial agriculture
Forests are cleared by burning and cultivated temporarily with low technology
nbe7e0dac253.x: Shifting cultivation is primitive subsistence farming, not capital-intensive export-oriented commercial agriculture.

n7459f5e728b.s: Which of the following pairs (type of farming – region) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Plantation farming – Malaysia, Brazil and India
Commercial grain farming – Prairies, Steppes, Pampas and Downs
n7459f5e728b.x: Mixed farming is associated with north-west Europe and eastern North America; Monsoon Asia is the region of intensive subsistence farming.

n41559420b64.s: Which of the following pairs (method – scholar) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Crop diversification – Bhatia, Jasbir Singh and Gibbs-Martin
Four macro agricultural regions of India – Sengupta and Sdasyuk
n41559420b64.x: Agricultural efficiency is associated with Kendall, Enyedi and Shafi; Sengupta and Sdasyuk gave the four macro agricultural regions.

nworld-geography-15-19.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
nworld-geography-15-19.s: Denmark, the Netherlands and New Zealand are noted for which type of farming?
nworld-geography-15-19.x: Dairy farming is practised in north-western Europe, Denmark, the Netherlands, New Zealand, the US Midwest and south-eastern Australia.

n5ae19370f71.s: Which of the following is an Old World crop?
n5ae19370f71.x: Coffee is an Old World crop; cocoa, rubber and chilli are New World crops.

n62c9d9e0ba2.s: The term 'Green Revolution' was coined in 1968 by:
n62c9d9e0ba2.x: William Gaud coined the term in 1968; Norman Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

n5a3f35f2e7e.s: Regions of Mediterranean agriculture receive most of their rainfall in:
n5a3f35f2e7e.x: Mediterranean regions get winter rain; viticulture, citrus and olives are typical.

ne68943325c0.x: Aquaponics combines soil-free hydroponics with fish rearing; neither is an agroecological practice.

n120b2b332d1.s: Mocha coffee is named after a port in:
n120b2b332d1.x: Mocha is an Arabica coffee named after the Yemeni port of Mocha; Arabica originated in Ethiopia.

n1f693f8f7a0.s: The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), which released IR8, is located in:
n1f693f8f7a0.x: IRRI (1960) is at Los Banos, Philippines; CIMMYT in Mexico works on maize and wheat.

n90736bdf8ba.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of cocoa?
n90736bdf8ba.x: Cote d'Ivoire is 1st and Ghana 2nd in cocoa.

nf0f71ba430c.x: Apiculture is bee-keeping; pisciculture is fish rearing, sericulture silk and viticulture grapes.

nworld-geography-3-7.s: Which country leads the world in copper production?
nworld-geography-3-7.x: Chile leads in copper; China leads in crude steel, Australia in iron ore and Brazil in coffee.

nworld-geography-15-7.s: Which of the following is NOT a region of commercial grain farming?
nworld-geography-15-7.x: The Prairies, Pampas and Steppes are grain regions; the Mediterranean Basin has Mediterranean farming.

nworld-geography-15-17.s: Mixed farming, as practised in Western Europe, the eastern USA and Argentina, combines:
o: two or more crops sown together
crops and livestock on the same farm
nworld-geography-15-17.x: Mixed farming combines crops and livestock on the same farm and is highly mechanised.

nworld-geography-15-5.s: Livestock ranching is a form of:
nworld-geography-15-5.x: Ranching is large-scale and commercial; nomadic herding involves seasonal migration for fodder and water.

nworld-geography-15-4.s: Which type of farming particularly requires refrigeration and transport?
nworld-geography-15-4.x: Dairy farming needs refrigeration and transport; Mediterranean agriculture specialises in olives, grapes and citrus.

nworld-geography-3-10.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of diamonds by value?
nworld-geography-3-10.x: Botswana leads by value, while Russia leads by volume.

nworld-geography-3-4.s: Which country is the world's largest exporter of rice?
nworld-geography-3-4.x: India is the largest rice exporter because it produces a large surplus over domestic consumption.

nworld-geography-15-11.s: Intensive subsistence farming, which gives a high yield per hectare, mainly relies on:
nworld-geography-15-11.x: Intensive subsistence farming uses family labour on small holdings and produces high yields per hectare.

nworld-geography-15-3.s: Plantation agriculture, an export-oriented monoculture, is a product of:
nworld-geography-15-3.x: Colonial estates were set up to grow one crop for export to the home country.

n985e7541f8d.s: Derwent Whittlesey's classification of world agricultural regions (1936) identified how many regions?

n9ea804cc3db.s: India's horticulture output, which now exceeds foodgrain output, is about:
n9ea804cc3db.x: Horticulture output is about 362–367 million tonnes and has surpassed foodgrain output.

n255872cb722.s: In which of the following crops does Andhra Pradesh rank first in India?
n255872cb722.x: AP ranks first in oil palm and is India's largest fruit producer; podu cultivation persists in its agency tracts.

n6798e38465d.s: Farming that applies high labour and capital input per unit of land is called:
n6798e38465d.x: Intensive farming uses high input per unit of land; extensive farming uses large areas with low input.

n571643b09c5.s: The core region of India's Green Revolution was:
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
n571643b09c5.x: The core region was Punjab, Haryana and western UP; M.S. Swaminathan and C. Subramaniam were key Indian figures.

n4c57088db52.s: Which of the following ICAR institutes is NOT correctly matched with its location?
o: Indian Institute of Rice Research – Hyderabad
Indian Institute of Pulses Research – Lucknow
Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research – Pedavegi (Eluru)
Indian Institute of Millets Research – Hyderabad
n4c57088db52.x: The Indian Institute of Pulses Research (former DPR) is at Kanpur, not Lucknow.

nindian-geography-24-29.s: Which of the following pairs (crop – growing condition) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Watermelon – hot summer of the Zaid season
Rice – high temperature and rainfall above 100 cm
Cotton – black soil and frost-free conditions
Wheat – hot summer of the Zaid season
nindian-geography-24-29.x: Wheat needs a cool growing season with relatively dry conditions; the hot Zaid summer suits watermelon.

naa64ec2268a.s: Wheat in India is chiefly associated with which group of States?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh
naa64ec2268a.x: Wheat is chiefly grown in UP, Punjab, Haryana and MP; rice is grown with both rainfall and irrigation in many States.

nbiology-22-9.s: Black rust of wheat is caused by:
nbiology-22-9.x: Black rust is caused by Puccinia graminis tritici; Ustilago causes loose smut, Sphaerulina narrow brown leaf spot and RTSV/RTBV rice tungro.

n1e29ce99474.s: Which millet is a drought-tolerant crop of hot, dry conditions, led by Rajasthan?
n1e29ce99474.x: Bajra suits hot, dry conditions on sandy soils and is led by Rajasthan; ragi is grown in peninsular India, especially Karnataka.

nworld-geography-21-6.s: Which country is the world's leading producer of maize?
nworld-geography-21-6.x: Maize runs USA > China > Brazil; wheat runs China > India > Russia.

ndeff8ef9b24.s: In 1970, Norman Borlaug, who developed Mexican dwarf wheat, received the Nobel Prize for:
ndeff8ef9b24.x: Borlaug received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970; M.S. Swaminathan is the father of India's Green Revolution and C. Subramaniam was the Union Agriculture Minister who backed it.

n53ae6ded292.s: The National Food Security Mission (NFSM) for rice, wheat and pulses was launched in:
n53ae6ded292.x: NFSM began in 2007-08; nutri-cereals were added in 2018-19.

n52fff645649.s: The Green Revolution helped India move towards food self-sufficiency from wheat imports under:
n52fff645649.x: India moved from PL-480 wheat imports towards self-sufficiency, though rainfed and hill areas remained neglected.

n2d3c05a9ffa.s: Sowing the next crop into the standing crop before it is harvested is called:
n2d3c05a9ffa.x: Relay cropping sows the next crop into the standing crop; ratoon cropping is regrowth from stubble and mixed cropping sows crops together without a row pattern.

ne0e07c1b76b.s: India, the largest rice exporter, accounts for about what share of world rice trade?
ne0e07c1b76b.x: India has about 40 per cent of world rice trade; its rice output (150.18 MT) has also surpassed China's.

n1d72c1cca90.s: Which millet contributes about 60 per cent of India's millet output?
n1d72c1cca90.x: Bajra (pearl millet) gives about 60 per cent of India's millet output; India produces 42.75 per cent of world millets.

n0f713a409f8.s: How many agro-climatic zones did the Planning Commission identify in the Seventh Plan?
n0f713a409f8.x: There are 15 agro-climatic zones based on soil, climate and cropping pattern, sub-divided into 72 sub-zones.

n37c0e24d78e.s: The first phase of the Green Revolution (mid-1960s to 1980s) was centred largely on:
n37c0e24d78e.x: Wheat was central to the first phase; rice benefited in a later, wider phase while pulses and coarse cereals lagged.

nindian-geography-22-51.s: The Directorate of Wheat Research was located at:
nindian-geography-22-51.x: Wheat Research was at Karnal, Rice Research at Hyderabad, Maize Research at New Delhi and Pulses Research at Kanpur.

ndb17f4fdd8b.s: BGREI (Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India) was launched in 2010-11 under:
ndb17f4fdd8b.x: BGREI was launched under RKVY for the rice-based cropping system of the eastern States.

nindian-geography-24-11.s: The approximate western limit of rice cultivation in India is marked by the:
nindian-geography-24-11.x: The 100 cm isohyet marks the western limit of rice; Uttar Pradesh had the largest rice area in 2024–25.

nworld-geography-15-24.s: 'Chena' is the name for shifting cultivation in:
nworld-geography-15-24.x: Chena is used in Sri Lanka; milpa in Central America and Mexico, conuco in Venezuela and tavy in Madagascar.

nindian-geography-24-27.x: Gram is a rabi pulse; moong is a kharif pulse, cotton a kharif fibre crop and cucumber a zaid crop.

nindian-geography-24-5.s: Which of the following is NOT a Rabi crop?
nindian-geography-24-5.x: Cucumber is a zaid crop; gram, mustard and lathyrus are rabi crops.

ne44535c39ef.s: Which factors have been identified as favouring rice–wheat cultivation, including paddy in Punjab?
o: Minimum Support Price and free power
ne44535c39ef.x: MSP arrangements and free power give rice and wheat policy advantages, favouring paddy in Punjab.

nworld-geography-21-7.s: The USA Corn Belt is a classic region of which crop?
nworld-geography-21-7.x: Maize grows in temperate and subtropical regions, the US Corn Belt being classic; wheat grows on the temperate grasslands.

nindian-geography-24-10.s: Rice requires a temperature of about:
nindian-geography-24-10.x: Rice needs about 25°C, rainfall above 100 cm and high humidity.

nindian-geography-24-4.s: Which of the following is a Zaid crop?
nindian-geography-24-4.x: Bitter gourd is zaid; peas and linseed are rabi and soybean is kharif.

n1839e1750de.s: Pulses are used in crop rotation because they:
n1839e1750de.x: Pulses are leguminous and fix atmospheric nitrogen, so they are used in rotation.

n94f8cfaf6d1.s: Agriculture in Andhra Pradesh is diversifying from food grains towards:
o: fruits, vegetables, spices and oil palm
n94f8cfaf6d1.x: AP is diversifying from food grains towards fruits, vegetables, spices and oil palm.

n06b56eb3dcb.s: India's net sown area in 2021-22 was about:
n06b56eb3dcb.x: Net sown area was 141 MH and gross cropped area 219.16 MH in 2021-22.

n841f091f7d5.s: India's record foodgrain production in 2024–25 was:
n841f091f7d5.x: Foodgrain output was 357.73 MT in 2024–25, while horticulture was higher at 367.72 MT.

nce92f0bfde1.s: Wheat, mainly a rabi crop, is the ____ most important cereal in India.
nce92f0bfde1.x: Wheat is India's second most important cereal; it is grown in the Ganga-Satluj plains and also the black-soil region of the Deccan.

n571b7211abf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about cash crops in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Chilli and tobacco are grown in the black-soil belt
Guntur is a major chilli-trade hub
AP ranks first in turmeric and second in chilli
The Tobacco Board is headquartered at Guntur
n571b7211abf.x: The ranks are reversed: AP ranks first in chilli and second in turmeric.

nebc836124b2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about plantation crops in India?
o: Tea needs about 20-30°C, 150-300 cm of rain and acidic, well-drained hill slopes
Rubber grows on the alluvial flood plains of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta with 50-70 cm of rain
Coffee needs about 15-28°C, shade and 150-250 cm of rain
Coffee needs deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil
nebc836124b2.x: Rubber needs a hot humid climate (25-35°C) with heavy rainfall; it is not a crop of the delta flood plains with 50-70 cm rain.

nworld-geography-21-18.s: Which of the following pairs (crop – requirement) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sugarcane – hot and humid conditions, heavy rain or irrigation, fertile soil
Tea – equatorial climate with over 200 cm of rainfall
Rubber – equatorial climate with over 200 cm of rainfall
nworld-geography-21-18.x: Tea needs moderate temperature, high rainfall and well-drained slopes; the equatorial climate with over 200 cm rain is rubber's requirement.

n98b9c9c97f9.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
n98b9c9c97f9.s: The sugarcane crushing season in the tropical belt of India runs from:
n98b9c9c97f9.x: The tropical crushing season is longer, October to May/June; November to February is the sub-tropical season.

nb4cdf4c3943.s: Under MIDH, the Centre-State funding ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States is:
nb4cdf4c3943.x: MIDH funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States; its sub-schemes include NHM, HMNEH and the National Bamboo Mission.

nf8d0b87e5ff.s: The Coconut Development Board (Kochi) functions under the:
nf8d0b87e5ff.x: It is under the Ministry of Agriculture; the Tea, Coffee, Rubber, Spices and Tobacco Boards are under the Department of Commerce.

nindian-geography-22-9.s: The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture is located at:
nindian-geography-22-9.x: Arid Horticulture is at Bikaner, Temperate at Srinagar, Subtropical at Lucknow, and Dr. Y.S. Parmar University at Solan.

nd7a15f29a3d.s: Plantation crops such as tea, coffee, rubber and coconut are generally:
nd7a15f29a3d.x: Plantation crops need substantial labour and capital; colonial plantations were European-dominated and export-oriented.

nindian-geography-17-4.x: The Round Revolution is potato; Black is petroleum, Pink is onion or meat and Brown is leather or non-conventional energy.

n2a3d4d6b0e5.s: Which of the following is a relatively water-efficient crop alternative in Indian agriculture?
n2a3d4d6b0e5.x: Millets, pulses and oilseeds are water-efficient; paddy in Punjab and sugarcane in Maharashtra reflect subsidy distortions.

nd0cf34deebb.s: Lakadong, a high-curcumin turmeric variety, belongs to:
nd0cf34deebb.x: Lakadong turmeric is from Meghalaya, which also leads in pineapple; Arunachal grows over half of India's kiwi.

n06c109a7535.s: The Rubber Board is headquartered at:
n06c109a7535.x: The Rubber Board is at Kottayam, the Coffee Board at Bengaluru, the Tea Board at Kolkata and the Spices Board at Kochi.

n644ec4bacf7.s: The NRC (National Research Centre) for Banana is located at:
n644ec4bacf7.x: NRC Banana is at Tiruchirappalli; IIHR is at Bengaluru, CISH at Lucknow and IIVR at Varanasi.

ndb24aa1ce2c.s: Sugarcane is a long-duration crop of about:
ndb24aa1ce2c.x: Sugarcane takes about 10-15 months, needs hot humid conditions and grows on alluvial or black soil.

n370fbea7b3b.s: The Araku coffee cluster is located in which State?
n370fbea7b3b.x: Araku and the ASR district are AP's coffee clusters; Kodagu is in Karnataka and the Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu.

n59017c9dfd8.s: The laterite soil of the Western Ghats is linked to which crop?
n59017c9dfd8.x: Laterite soil is linked to rubber; jute grows on alluvial flood plains, and black soils suit cotton, chillies and tobacco.

n6244a16f836.s: Indian jute goods face export competition mainly from:
n6244a16f836.x: Bangladesh competes with Indian jute goods in exports, while cotton competes with synthetic fibres.

nworld-geography-21-5.s: Which country is the world's leading producer of jute?
nworld-geography-21-5.x: India is the leading jute producer, followed by Bangladesh.

nworld-geography-21-17.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of tobacco?
nworld-geography-21-17.x: Tobacco production runs China > India > Brazil, with the USA also among the top.

o: integrated development of agriculture and allied sectors
nindian-geography-17-3.x: The Rainbow Revolution combines the Green, White, Blue and other coloured revolutions for integrated growth of agriculture and allied sectors.

nworld-geography-21-16.s: Which is a major jute-producing delta region of the world?
nworld-geography-21-16.x: Jute grows in hot, humid deltas, which is why the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta leads.

n3f2ec9da1db.s: Which of the following is a major cotton-producing State of India?
n3f2ec9da1db.x: The major cotton States are Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, mainly in black-soil regions.

nworld-geography-21-3.s: Sugar mills are located near the cane fields because sugarcane is a:
nworld-geography-21-3.x: Cane loses weight and sugar after cutting, so mills are located near the fields.
